chapters.summary: On the plains east of the Jordan, Moses reviews for the Israelites their journey from Sinai to Kadesh-barnea, reaffirms God's promises and commands, and recounts the lesson of how their unbelief kept them out of Canaan.
keyPoints: East of the Jordan, Moses spoke God's words to the Israelites, reviewing their journey from Horeb to Kadesh-barnea.
God promised to give Israel the land of Canaan and commanded them to go up and take possession of it, but the people refused out of fear.
Because of the people's unbelief and complaining, God swore that none of that generation would enter the land, except Caleb and Joshua.
chapters.application: Remember how God has led you in the past, and don't let present difficulties make you doubt his promises. Take the next step in faith, trusting that he will accomplish what he has promised.

chapters.summary: This chapter records how the Israelites journeyed through the wilderness, passing by the territories of the descendants of Esau and the Moabites and Ammonites—whom God told them not to disturb—and began their conquest of Sihon king of the Amorites, preparing to enter the promised land.
keyPoints: Following God's instructions, the Israelites went around Mount Seir and did not fight against the descendants of Esau.
God had given Ar and the surrounding territory to the Moabites, so the Israelites were not to harass them.
The Israelites defeated Sihon king of the Amorites and took his land, demonstrating God's faithfulness.
chapters.application: In the wilderness seasons of life, wait patiently for God's timing, respect the boundaries he sets for others, and trust that he will lead us into the abundant place he has prepared.

chapters.summary: Moses recalls Israel's defeat of Og king of Bashan, the allotment of the land east of the Jordan to two and a half tribes, and his charge to Joshua to be strong and courageous.
keyPoints: The Israelites defeated Og king of Bashan and captured sixty of his cities.
Moses gave the land east of the Jordan to Reuben, Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh.
Moses charged Joshua not to be afraid, for the LORD himself would fight for him.
chapters.application: Looking back at how God has led us in the past strengthens our confidence for what lies ahead. Whatever the road before us today, let us be strong and courageous, for God will be with us.

chapters.summary: Moses urges the Israelites to keep God's statutes and ordinances, warns them against idolatry, calls them to know the one true God, and warns of the consequences of rebellion.
keyPoints: Moses reaffirms the importance of the law, for those who obey it will live.
He warns against carving idols, for the LORD their God is a consuming fire, a jealous God.
He calls Israel to know God's faithfulness and to seek him in times of distress.
chapters.application: Today, let us make God's word the standard for our lives, turn away from every idol, and seek him wholeheartedly in hardship, that we may experience his mercy and deliverance.

chapters.summary: Moses reaffirms the Ten Commandments, urging the Israelites to keep them carefully and to obey God with reverent fear.
keyPoints: Moses assembled the Israelites and reaffirmed the covenant God had made at Sinai.
The Ten Commandments were the heart of God's covenant with his people, requiring their complete loyalty.
Keeping the commandments would bring a blessed life, and they were to be passed down to the next generation.
chapters.application: Today, let us receive God's word with reverence, put our faith into practice in daily life, and teach the next generation, so that our whole family may be blessed.

chapters.summary: Moses urges the Israelites to keep God's commandments, to love him with all their heart, and to teach their children to obey, so that they may be blessed and live long in the land.
keyPoints: Fear the LORD and keep all his commandments, so that you and your children after you may be blessed.
Love the LORD your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your strength, and keep his words upon your heart.
Teach these words diligently to your children, talking about them whether you sit at home, walk along the road, lie down, or rise up.
chapters.application: Today, let love for God be the center of our lives. Let us treasure his word in our hearts and diligently teach the next generation, so that our faith is passed down from one generation to the next.

chapters.summary: This chapter tells how God commanded the Israelites to thoroughly destroy the idols and nations of Canaan, and promised that if they kept his commandments, he would bless and protect them.
keyPoints: The Israelites had to utterly destroy the seven nations of Canaan and were not to make treaties with them or intermarry with them, lest they be led astray from God.
Israel was chosen not because of their own righteousness, but because of God's promise to their forefathers and his faithfulness.
God promised that if they kept his commandments, he would bless their numbers, their harvests, and their health, and protect them from their enemies.
chapters.application: Let us remove from our lives anything that hinders our closeness to God, rely wholeheartedly on his faithfulness, and obey his word, so that we may experience his blessing and protection.

chapters.summary: Moses reminds the Israelites to remember God's guidance and discipline in the wilderness, warning them not to forget God once they prosper and grow proud.
keyPoints: God humbled Israel in the wilderness and tested them, to see whether they would keep his commandments.
God fed them with manna to teach them that man does not live on bread alone, but on every word that comes from the mouth of the LORD.
The people were warned not to forget God or boast in their own wealth and strength, but to remember that it was he who gave them the power to prosper.
chapters.application: In times of prosperity, remember God's grace, keep a humble heart, and obey his commands, so that we do not forget him.

chapters.summary: Moses reminds the Israelites that their victory and the land they receive are not due to their own righteousness but to God's grace and promise, and he recounts their repeated history of rebellion.
keyPoints: God would drive out nations greater and stronger than Israel, but they were not to become proud, for the victory was God's doing.
God gave them the land not because of Israel's righteousness, but because of the wickedness of the Canaanite nations and his promise to their forefathers.
Moses recalled Israel's rebellions in the wilderness, such as the golden calf, proving that they were a stiff-necked people.
chapters.application: Our salvation and blessing rest entirely on God's grace, not because we are better than others. Let us remain humble and grateful, avoid pride, and always remember God's faithfulness.

chapters.summary: This chapter tells how Moses made new stone tablets, reaffirms God's call for Israel to fear him and walk in his ways, and emphasizes God's care for the orphan, the widow, and the foreigner.
keyPoints: At God's command, Moses cut new stone tablets, on which the Ten Commandments were written again, and placed them in the ark.
God chose the tribe of Levi to serve him, and reaffirmed that Israel was to fear him and keep his commandments.
God is God of gods, great and mighty, yet he loves justice and cares for the orphan, the widow, and the foreigner.
chapters.application: Let us live in reverent fear of God, walk in his ways, and imitate his justice and compassion by caring for those in need around us, putting our faith into practice.

chapters.summary: Moses urges the Israelites to love God and keep his commandments, promising blessing for obedience and disaster for rebellion.
keyPoints: Love the LORD your God, and always keep his charge, his statutes, his ordinances, and his commandments.
Pay careful attention to God's commandments and serve him with all your heart and all your soul, and he will send the autumn and spring rains in their season.
Moses set before the Israelites a blessing and a curse, calling them to choose obedience.
chapters.application: Today, let love for God be our motivation to obey his word. Believing that obedience brings blessing and rebellion brings discipline, let us make the right choices in our daily lives.

chapters.summary: This chapter instructs the Israelites that once they entered Canaan, they were to worship only at the place God would choose, and were strictly forbidden to follow the worship practices of the nations.
keyPoints: They were to thoroughly destroy the Canaanites' altars, sacred pillars, and idols, and not imitate their worship.
They were to offer sacrifices and rejoice only at the place God chose, not wherever they pleased.
They were not to eat blood, but were to keep the feasts before the LORD and carefully obey all his commandments.
chapters.application: Today, let us worship God in spirit and truth, turn away from the idols and customs of the world, and be united in the church in obeying God's word, enjoying true and lasting joy.

chapters.summary: This chapter warns the Israelites not to be led astray by false prophets, dreamers, or even close relatives into serving other gods, and calls them to root out such evil completely and remain faithful to the LORD.
keyPoints: Even if a false prophet or dreamer performs a sign or wonder, if he leads people away from God he must not be heeded, but put to death.
If a close relative or friend secretly entices someone to serve other gods, that person must show no pity but must put the offender to death with their own hand.
If a city's inhabitants were led astray to serve other gods, the matter had to be thoroughly investigated and, if true, the city utterly destroyed.
chapters.application: Today, let us be on guard against anything that would lead us away from the truth, even if it seems miraculous or comes from someone close to us, and let God's word remain our standard as we hold fast to our faith.

chapters.summary: This chapter teaches that as God's holy people, the Israelites were to be set apart in what they ate and what they offered, and not follow the customs of the nations.
keyPoints: They were forbidden to cut themselves or shave their heads for the dead, for they were children of God and were to be holy.
Clean and unclean animals were to be distinguished, marking out what could and could not be eaten.
The tithe was to be eaten before the LORD, and was also to provide for the Levites, the foreigner, the orphan, and the widow.
chapters.application: Let us live set apart for God in every area of life, and give willingly, responding in action to his choosing of us and becoming a blessing to others.

chapters.summary: This chapter instructs the Israelites to release debts in the year of release and to help the poor generously, reminding them that obedience to God brings blessing.
keyPoints: At the end of every seven years, they were to grant a release, canceling the debts owed by their fellow Israelites.
They were to help their poor brothers generously, without a grudging heart.
Willing obedience to God would bring blessing, so that Israel would prosper above all nations.
chapters.application: Today, let us help those in need with a generous heart, trusting that God will supply all that we need.

chapters.summary: This chapter reaffirms the regulations for Israel's three great feasts—Passover, the Feast of Weeks, and the Feast of Tabernacles—emphasizing worship at the place God would choose, and it establishes judges and officials to administer justice fairly.
keyPoints: The Passover was to be kept at the place God chose, sacrificing there in remembrance of the exodus from Egypt.
The Feast of Weeks called for a freewill offering, given in proportion to how God had blessed them.
The Feast of Tabernacles was to be kept for seven days, and fair judges were to be appointed.
chapters.application: In daily life, let us remember God's salvation with a grateful heart, pursue fairness and integrity, and treat others well, so that our faith is expressed in everyday action.

chapters.summary: Deuteronomy 17 instructs the Israelites concerning unblemished sacrifices, fair judgment, and regulations for kingship, emphasizing complete obedience to God's law.
keyPoints: Sacrificial animals had to be without defect, for offering a blemished animal was detestable to the LORD.
Anyone who worshiped false gods was to be condemned only on the testimony of two or three witnesses, and the witnesses had to be the first to carry out the execution, to root out evil.
A king had to be one whom God chose, and he was to copy out the law and read it all the days of his life, so that his heart would not become proud.
chapters.application: In daily life, let us give to God with a wholehearted spirit, honor his law, and pursue fairness and humility in all things, so that our lives are pleasing to him.

chapters.summary: This chapter teaches that the LORD himself is the Levites' inheritance, warns Israel not to imitate the detestable practices of the nations, and promises that God would raise up a prophet like Moses.
keyPoints: The Levites had no inheritance of land, for the LORD was their portion, and the priests were to receive their share of the offerings.
The Israelites were not to practice divination, sorcery, or other detestable practices, but were to be wholly devoted to God.
God promised to raise up a prophet like Moses, whom the people were to heed, while any false prophet was to be put to death.
chapters.application: Let us regard God as our true inheritance and support, staying far from every superstition and occult practice, listening carefully to his word, and living as a holy witness.

chapters.summary: This chapter establishes cities of refuge to protect those who kill someone by accident, and gives strict warnings against moving boundary markers or bearing false witness, emphasizing fair judgment.
keyPoints: Three cities of refuge were established, so that anyone who killed another by accident could flee there for safety from the avenger of blood.
No one was to move a neighbor's boundary marker, protecting property rights and preventing encroachment.
False witnesses were to be severely punished, life for life, to ensure justice and purge evil from the community.
chapters.application: In life, let us be honest and trustworthy, not covet what belongs to others, and seek fair resolution when conflicts arise, while showing mercy and giving those who err a chance to change.

chapters.summary: This chapter gives the regulations for the Israelites when going to war, including the priest's words of encouragement, the officers' exemptions, and the principles for besieging a city.
keyPoints: Before battle, the priest declared God's presence and urged the people not to be afraid.
The officers announced exemptions from service for anyone who had just married, built a new house, or planted a vineyard.
Before besieging a city, they were to offer it terms of peace; if refused, they were to act according to God's instructions, and even then were to spare the fruit trees.
chapters.application: In the battles of life, trust in God rather than our own strength, and act with wisdom and mercy, carrying out his principles in what we do.

chapters.summary: This chapter gives regulations concerning an unsolved murder, a captive woman taken as a wife, the rights of the firstborn, and the treatment of a rebellious son, emphasizing holiness and justice.
keyPoints: If a slain body was found, the elders and judges were to measure the distance to the nearest town, and its elders, with the priests, were to perform an atonement ritual with a heifer, seeking God's forgiveness.
A man who took a captive woman as his wife had to allow her a month to mourn, and if he later no longer delighted in her, he had to let her go free, not sell her as a slave.
The rights of the firstborn could not be shifted because of favoritism, and a rebellious son was to be brought before the elders and stoned to death, to purge evil from Israel.
chapters.application: Today, let us pursue fairness, honor order within the family, discipline our children with love, and rely on God as we work through difficulties in our relationships.

chapters.summary: Deuteronomy 22 teaches the Israelites regulations concerning love for neighbor, ritual distinctions, and marital faithfulness, emphasizing the importance of holy living.
keyPoints: If they saw a fellow Israelite's ox or sheep wandering astray, they were not to ignore it but were to bring it back to its owner.
A woman was not to wear men's clothing, nor a man wear women's clothing, for this was detestable to the LORD.
If a man married a woman and then found evidence she was not a virgin, the matter had to be handled according to the law, to purge evil from Israel.
chapters.application: Today, let us care for our neighbor's needs with love, hold fast to holiness in our lives, honor marriage, and glorify God.

chapters.summary: Deuteronomy 23 sets out regulations concerning eligibility for the assembly, cleanliness of the camp, receiving runaway slaves, the prohibition of temple prostitution, lending at interest, fulfilling vows, and entering a neighbor's vineyard, emphasizing that Israel was to be a holy community.
keyPoints: The emasculated, those born of a forbidden union, and Ammonites and Moabites could not enter the assembly of the LORD, but the third generation of Edomites and Egyptians could.
The Israelite camp had to remain clean, since God himself walked among them, and anything unclean was to be kept far away.
Cult prostitution was forbidden, interest was not to be charged on loans to fellow Israelites, vows had to be kept, and anyone entering a neighbor's vineyard could eat there but not carry fruit away.
chapters.application: Let us pursue a holy life, since God is present among us, while also showing compassion to outsiders and remaining honest and trustworthy in all things, to God's glory.

chapters.summary: This chapter instructs the Israelites in regulations concerning divorce, newlyweds, lending, and hired workers—matters of social justice and mercy—emphasizing that God cares about people's needs and dignity.
keyPoints: Divorce required a certificate, to prevent a wife being sent away carelessly and to uphold the seriousness of marriage.
A newly married man was exempted from military service and public duty for a year, so the couple could enjoy their marriage and give priority to family.
Hired workers, foreigners, orphans, and widows were not to be oppressed, but their needs were to be cared for.
chapters.application: In everyday life, let us honor marriage, treat others well, and pay special attention to the poor and vulnerable, treating people with justice and compassion so that God's love is made visible.

chapters.summary: Deuteronomy 25 records regulations concerning fair judgment, a brother's duty to provide an heir for his deceased brother, and honest trade, emphasizing that Israel was to uphold fairness and kindness within the community.
keyPoints: Punishment was to fit the offense, but a beating could not exceed forty lashes, so that a fellow Israelite would not be degraded.
If a man died without a son, his brother was to marry the widow and raise up an heir for the deceased, fulfilling his duty as kinsman-redeemer.
Honest weights and measures were to be used in trade, without dishonest double standards, so as not to offend the LORD.
chapters.application: In everyday life, let us treat others with justice and honesty, fulfilling our responsibilities to family and neighbor, for God sees everything and delights when we act justly and love mercy.

chapters.summary: This chapter instructs the Israelites that once they entered the promised land, they were to offer the firstfruits of the land to God, acknowledging his saving acts and blessing throughout their history, and it reaffirms the importance of keeping his commandments.
keyPoints: When offering the firstfruits, they were to recite the history of how God led their forefathers down to Egypt and then delivered them out.
They were to acknowledge before God that all they had was his gift, and to give a tenth to the Levites and to the foreigner.
God would look down from heaven and bless his people, making them a holy people who kept his commandments.
chapters.application: Today, let us keep a grateful heart, remember God's grace, give willingly, and carefully keep his word, so that our lives become a testimony of his blessing.

chapters.summary: Moses instructs the Israelites that once they entered the land of Canaan, they were to set up stones inscribed with the law on Mount Ebal, and he declares blessing for those who keep the commandments and a curse for those who break them.
keyPoints: The Israelites were commanded that after crossing the Jordan, they were to set up large stones, coat them with plaster, and write the law on them.
They were to build an altar of stones on Mount Ebal and offer sacrifices there, using no iron tool, to show the purity of true worship.
The Levites pronounced the curses aloud, and the people answered "Amen," underscoring the seriousness of the law.
chapters.application: Today, let us receive God's word with reverence, not merely hearing it but doing it, obeying God in every part of life, turning away from sin, and receiving his blessing.

chapters.summary: This chapter records Moses declaring to the Israelites the blessings that would come from obeying God and the curses that would come from disobeying him, emphasizing the importance of keeping the commandments.
keyPoints: Obedience to God would bring blessing in the city and in the field, with blessing on their children, their land, and their livestock.
Disobedience would bring curses, including disease, drought, defeat in battle, and exile.
The Israelites were warned that if they forsook God, they would suffer terrible disaster, even being scattered among the nations.
chapters.application: Let us obey God's word with a willing heart, trusting his promises in daily life, turning away from sin, and experiencing his blessing and presence.

chapters.summary: In the land of Moab, Moses reaffirms the covenant, calling the Israelites to carefully keep God's commandments and avoid the curse that comes from idolatry.
keyPoints: Moses reviewed God's guidance and provision in the wilderness, reminding the people to recognize his mighty acts.
He declared that the covenant applied to everyone standing there that day, emphasizing that it extended across the generations.
He warned that the sin of idolatry would surely bring a curse, and urged the people to turn to God wholeheartedly.
chapters.application: Today, let us remember God's grace, turn away from every idol, and live obediently within his covenant, becoming a testimony of his blessing.

chapters.summary: Moses urges the Israelites that if they repent and turn back to God, he will restore them and cleanse their hearts, and he emphasizes that keeping the commandment is not too difficult, for it is near them—in their mouth and in their heart.
keyPoints: If, after being exiled, they repented and turned back to God, he would have mercy and gather them back.
God would circumcise their hearts, enabling them to love him with all their heart and all their soul, and so live.
The commandment was not far off but near, a matter of the mouth confessing and the heart believing, and they were to choose life and blessing.
chapters.application: Today, though we are not facing exile, we still know weakness and wandering. Let us turn back to God, for he will receive and renew us. May we choose obedience each day and live within his blessing.

chapters.summary: Near the end of his life, Moses encourages the people and Joshua, declares God's presence and the ongoing transmission of the law, and foretells Israel's future rebellion.
keyPoints: Moses declared that he was now old and that Joshua would lead the people into the promised land.
Moses commanded that the law be read aloud every seven years, so that the people would fear God and obey it.
God foretold that Israel would turn away from him, but promised that even amid disaster he would not abandon them.
chapters.application: Facing turning points in life, let us be like Joshua—relying on God's promises and being strong and courageous, for he will never leave us.

chapters.summary: In a song, Moses bears witness to God's faithfulness and Israel's rebellion, calling the people to remember his mighty acts and turn back to him in repentance.
keyPoints: Moses called heaven and earth to be witnesses, declaring that God's words fall like rain and dew that nourish the earth.
He recounted God's faithfulness and righteousness, contrasting it with Israel's crooked and perverse ways.
He prophesied that God's chosen people would suffer disaster for forsaking him, but that God would in the end vindicate his people.
chapters.application: Let us remember God's grace in our lives and never forget his mighty works. Let us give thanks in good times and turn back to him in hard times, for he is a righteous and loving God.

chapters.summary: Near the end of his life, Moses blesses each of the tribes of Israel, foretelling the blessing and calling that await them.
keyPoints: Moses began by recalling the majesty of God's appearing at Sinai, praising his law and his care for his people.
He blessed each tribe in turn—Reuben, Judah, Levi, Benjamin, and the others—highlighting each one's character and blessing.
He closed by calling Israel a blessed people, for God was their help and shield, giving them a place to dwell in safety.
chapters.application: Like Moses, let us bless others at every stage of life, and be confident that God is our everlasting help and shield, giving us peace.

chapters.summary: Moses views the promised land from Mount Nebo before he dies, Joshua takes up the leadership, and the Israelites mourn and remember Moses.
keyPoints: Moses climbed Mount Nebo and saw the whole land that God had promised to Israel.
Moses died in the land of Moab, and God himself buried him, so that to this day no one knows the location of his grave.
Joshua was chosen by God to succeed Moses, and the Israelites listened to him and honored him.
chapters.application: When one stage of life comes to an end, let us trust God's plan, for he will raise up new leaders to continue fulfilling his promises.
